essays.title: The Apostolic and Sub-Apostolic Age
essays.blurb: From Pentecost to the generation after the apostles. How a scattered, persecuted movement stayed one body across distance, and what held it together before the New Testament was gathered.

essays.title: The Age of the Martyrs
essays.blurb: From Nero's fire to Diocletian's last storm. What Rome actually demanded, why believers died rather than comply, and what the church learned about mercy from the people who failed.

essays.title: The Desert and the Rule
essays.blurb: Antony walked out of a village church and into the desert, and monasticism was born. How the church kept a full-price faith on offer once believing became easy, and what Benedict built from it.

essays.title: The Constantinian Turn
essays.blurb: A cross in the sky in 312, and the church woke up favored. What it gained, what it traded, and why the question it raised has never closed.

essays.title: The Fathers at Work
essays.blurb: The councils wrote the creeds, but the doctrine was carried between the meetings, in exiles, letters, famine relief, and one long fight over grace. The people who did the work.

essays.title: The Great Councils
essays.blurb: Nicaea, Constantinople, Ephesus, Chalcedon. The pastoral and political pressures behind the church's defining decisions about Christ and God, told as a human story.

essays.title: The Church That Outlived Rome
essays.blurb: Rome fell and the church did not. Slaves, monks, queens, and grieving scholars carried the faith to the peoples who broke the empire, and by the year 1000 Europe was baptized. What kind of victory that was is the harder question.

essays.title: The East and West Divide
essays.blurb: The slow drift between Greek East and Latin West. Language, authority, the disputed clause in the creed, and the events of 1054. Told fairly to both sides.

essays.title: The Medieval West
essays.blurb: From the reforming monks to the eve of Wittenberg. Papal power at its height, the cathedrals and the universities, the crusades and the inquisition, and the long refusal of reform that made Luther possible.

essays.title: The Reformation
essays.blurb: Luther and the German movement, the Reformed stream, the Radical wing, the English settlement, and the Catholic response. Honest about the recovery and about the violence and division.

essays.title: The Counter-Reformation and the Wars of Religion
essays.blurb: Rome's answer to the Protestant break, told fairly. Trent and the Jesuits, the saints of a real renewal, and the century of blood from the French massacres to Westphalia that ended Christendom.

essays.title: The Awakenings and the Birth of Evangelicalism
essays.blurb: Pietism, Edwards, Whitefield, and the Wesleys. How revival remade the faith of the English-speaking world, with the ledger of the revivalists and slavery kept open and honest.

essays.title: The Missionary Century
essays.blurb: From Carey's sailing to Edinburgh 1910. How the gospel reached every continent, what it owed and paid to empire, and the local believers who did most of the work.

essays.title: The Modern Church and the Global Shift
essays.blurb: The fundamentalist and modernist split, the churches under the dictators, Barmen and Bonhoeffer, the fire from Azusa Street, and the great reversal that moved the faith's center south.

essays.title: The Apostolic and Persecuted Church
essays.blurb: Three centuries with no buildings, no legal standing, and no cultural power — and the church grew anyway. What the first Christians had that we keep trying to buy.

essays.title: Councils and Creeds
essays.blurb: The empire stopped killing the church and started smiling at it. What the bishops protected at Nicaea and Chalcedon — and what the favor of Constantine began to cost.
